rationale: This benchmark is dominated by hot, tightly-unrolled loops (test_for/while/do/goto_loop_unroll at ~2KB each) in a timing-sensitive Adobe C++ SingleSource workload, so the table maximizes reverse-engineering resistance from low-cost structural transforms while throttling the loop-amplifying passes: SUB and SPLIT carry high diversity weights with minimal runtime/size cost and near-zero correctness risk, making them safe to apply broadly across the 292 functions; IBR adds cheap opaque-predicate-based branch diversity well suited to the branch-heavy loop bodies; IGV is favored for its global variable indirection (strong against static data-flow recovery) at low size cost; BCF and FLA are given high SecurityGain but the highest RuntimeCost weights so the selector applies them selectively only to functions whose features indicate low execution frequency (e.g., setup/test-harness code in simple_types_* and stepanov_* rather than the inner loops of loop_unroll.cpp), since bogus control flow and flattening compound multiplicatively inside already-unrolled hot loops; ICALL is kept moderate — indirect-call conversion degrades call-graph recovery but adds dispatch overhead and moderate correctness risk (varargs, attribute-sensitive calls) that is not worth paying inside the timer-measured kernels; CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low everywhere except FLA/ICALL to preserve the benchmark's required numerical outputs.
